name: Conrad Tao Piano

why: Free outdoor Halloween screening of Diablo Cody's 2009 cult horror-comedy.

name: Scientific Controversies: Octopus Umwelt
why: Scientists debate the sensory world of octopuses and what it means to perceive differently from humans.

name: Astronomy Live: Cosmic Building Blocks
why: Live astronomy program exploring the fundamental elements that make up the cosmos.

name: Creative Showcase Vol. 7 (Pecha Kucha Format)
why: Pecha kucha-format showcase featuring seven creatives sharing work across art, design, and culture.

name: Fantastic Fiction at KGB

name: Peer Revue at Caveat
why: Scientists and researchers share funny stories from their work in a variety show format.

name: Outdoor Movie: Practical Magic at Prospect Park
why: Free outdoor Halloween-season screening of the 1998 witch-sister romantic fantasy.

name: Infinite Good Times: John Carpenter Double Feature
why: Free double feature of John Carpenter horror films at a neighborhood bar.

name: Sunnyside Horror Society: The Exorcist (Weekly Wednesdays)
why: Weekly horror film screenings every Wednesday through Oct 28; Oct 14 showing: The Exorcist.

name: ICP New Exhibitions: I'm So Happy You Are Here + Laia Abril
why: Two exhibitions open Oct 15 through Jan 11, 2027: Japanese women photographers in 'I'm So Happy You Are Here' and Laia Abril's expanded body work.

name: HONK! NYC Festival

name: BBG Fall Plant Sale
why: Annual fall plant sale with native plants, bulbs, and houseplants from BBG's horticulture team.

name: NY Classical Players: Beethoven 200 in Clinton Hill
why: Chamber concert celebrating the 200th anniversary of Beethoven's last completed string quartets.

name: Facts Machine: Spooky Science at Caveat
why: Science trivia and variety show with a Halloween spooky-science theme.

name: Outdoor Movie: Scooby-Doo at Sunset Park
why: Free outdoor Halloween-season screening of the 2002 live-action Scooby-Doo film.

name: Top Shelf Stories at UCB

name: It Entirely From Memory
why: Live show where performers recreate films, TV shows, and albums entirely from memory, errors included.

name: Footlight's Undead Prom

name: Chelsea Film Festival
why: Annual international film festival running Oct 14–18 at Regal Battery Park.

name: Urbanworld Film Festival
why: Annual film festival celebrating works by and about underrepresented communities, running Oct 14–18.

name: Brooklyn Horror Film Festival
why: Annual horror film festival running Oct 15–22 at Nitehawk Cinema and Prospect Park.

name: Newfest: NY LGBTQ+ Film Festival
why: Annual LGBTQ+ film festival running Oct 15–25 at various NYC venues.

name: Open by Design: NYC Developer Meetup w/ Together AI, NVIDIA, Reflection AI
why: Developer meetup with Together AI, NVIDIA, and Reflection AI exploring open-source AI infrastructure and model development.

name: The Next Frontier of AI Agents w/ Prior Labs + Mistral
why: Panel on the next frontier of agentic AI systems with Prior Labs and Mistral researchers.

name: Exhibition Panel: Primers for a Handmade Utopia
why: Panel discussion accompanying the 'Primers for a Handmade Utopia' exhibition exploring design, craft, and utopian visions.

name: Kelly Walters for Open Flat File Lecture
why: Designer and educator Kelly Walters presents her practice for the Open Flat File lecture series.

name: Sawyer Avenue, Sunday Afternoon — Film Screening + Panel
why: Screening of Sawyer Avenue, Sunday Afternoon followed by a panel discussion.

name: Praise Day for Sonia Sanchez!
why: Celebration of poet and activist Sonia Sanchez with readings, tributes, and performances.

name: In the Room: David Hume Kennerly — Sixty Years on the Front Line of History
why: Pulitzer Prize-winning photojournalist David Hume Kennerly reflects on six decades covering major world events.

name: Beaux Arts Ball 2026: Home Sweet Home
why: Annual Beaux Arts Ball fundraiser gala with the theme 'Home Sweet Home' at the historic Andrew Freedman Home in the Bronx.

name: From Field to Form: Ocean Flora — Panel on Marine Building Materials
why: Panel exploring the use of marine algae and ocean flora as sustainable building materials and architectural elements.

name: Art Deco Washington Heights Walking Tour
why: Guided walking tour exploring Art Deco architecture in Washington Heights with MAS docents.

name: Grand Central Terminal Walking Tour
why: Recurring guided tour of Grand Central Terminal's architecture, history, and hidden spaces with MAS docents; multiple dates available.

name: Free Preview Screening: Making Marie Antoinette
why: Free preview of Eleanor Coppola's 2026 documentary made from 80 hours of footage she shot while watching daughter Sofia direct Marie Antoinette at Versailles in 2005.

name: Marie Antoinette 20th Anniversary 4K Restoration
why: Theatrical screening of Sofia Coppola's Marie Antoinette in a new 20th anniversary 4K restoration.

name: OHNY Launch Party at the Woolworth Building
why: OHNY Weekend kickoff party inside the ornate lobby of the Cass Gilbert-designed Woolworth Building.

name: OHNY Weekend 2026 — Open House New York
why: Annual architecture and design festival Oct 16–18 with free drop-in access to 150+ landmarks, studios, labs, and spaces across all five boroughs.

name: New York: A Documentary Film — Episode 9 (with Ric Burns & James Sanders)
why: First full public screening of Episode 9 of the PBS docuseries New York: A Documentary Film, covering the city's second half of the 20th century, followed by Q&A with director Ric Burns.

name: New York: A Documentary Film — Episode 10 (with Ric Burns & James Sanders)
why: First full public screening of Episode 10 of the PBS docuseries New York: A Documentary Film, covering post-9/11 NYC through today, followed by Q&A with director Ric Burns.

name: Performance: What Season Is It, America?
why: Multi-day performance installation running Wed–Sun Oct 21–25 exploring American identity and season as metaphor.

name: Convening: In Pursuit of Life, Liberty, and Happiness
why: Day-long convening program exploring questions of civic life, justice, and what it means to pursue happiness in contemporary America.

name: Sculpting the (Un)Spoken: Participatory Performance with Iris van Herpen
why: Three-day participatory performance by fashion designer Iris van Herpen running Oct 30–Nov 1 in connection with her Brooklyn Museum retrospective.

name: Exhibition: Bonded for Life — Billie Jean King and Elton John
why: New installation using garments, ephemera, and photographs to celebrate Billie Jean King and Elton John's decades-long friendship and shared activism for LGBTQ+ rights and gender parity.

name: Gallery Tour: Revolutionary Women
why: Docent-led tour of the Revolutionary Women galleries at NY Historical.

name: Gallery Tour: Democracy Matters
why: Docent-led tour exploring the Democracy Matters galleries.

name: William Howard Taft: A Great American Life
why: Biographer Walter Stahr and Jeffrey Rosen discuss William Howard Taft's legacy before and after the presidency.

name: BeBop Porú: Free Dance Party (Homecoming: For the Harbor)
why: All-day free outdoor dance party featuring global Black American dance music fused with Caribbean and South American rhythms by DJ Mickey Pérez and DJ L3Ni, 2–8pm.

name: Flagpole Piñata Party
why: Festive piñata party on Governors Island as part of the final fall weekend of the 2026 season.

name: Pumpkin Point 2026
why: Fall pumpkin patch and Halloween activities on Governors Island through late October.

name: 2026 Louis Auchincloss Prize Honoring Colson Whitehead
venue: Museum of the City of New York
source: Museum of the City of New York
via: Museum of the City of New York
why: Public program presenting the Louis Auchincloss Prize to two-time Pulitzer winner Colson Whitehead, moderated by Wesley Morris of the New York Times.

name: Raise Your Voice: Curator-led Tour of NYC Social Movements
venue: Museum of the City of New York
source: Museum of the City of New York
via: Museum of the City of New York
why: Monthly curator-led tour exploring objects and tools behind NYC social movements in the 'Raise Your Voice: New York Activism' exhibition, part of Free Late-Night Wednesdays.

name: Movie Under the Stars: Practical Magic (1998) at Prospect Park
why: Free outdoor screening of the 1998 Halloween-season classic Practical Magic in Prospect Park.

name: Thursday Classic Movie Night: A Shriek In The Night (1933)
venue: Herbert Von King Cultural Arts Center, Herbert Von King Park
why: Free indoor screening of the 1933 pre-Code mystery-horror 'A Shriek In The Night' at the Von King Arts Center in Bed-Stuy.

name: Shelter and Reconstruction After Earthquakes in Türkiye and Japan
why: Architects and engineers discuss reconstruction strategies and lessons learned after the 2023 Türkiye and recent Japan earthquakes.

name: The Bloomsbury Global Encyclopedia of Women in Architecture, 1960-2020
why: Panel discussion on the first comprehensive survey of women in architecture worldwide, featuring the editors and contributors to the new encyclopedia.

name: n+1 Magazine Presents: The Municipal Sublime
why: n+1 magazine and the Center for Architecture discuss the idea of the Municipal Sublime—the poetry and politics of public infrastructure.

name: Archtober Walking Tour: The Architecture of Madison Square Park
why: Archtober walking tour exploring the architecture and monuments surrounding Madison Square Park, from the Flatiron Building to the Met Life Tower.

name: Archtober Walking Tour: Privately Owned Public Spaces (POPS) in Midtown North
why: Archtober tour exploring Midtown's lesser-known privately owned public spaces—plazas, atriums, and arcades legally accessible to the public.

name: Exhibition: Humanist Modernity — Maciej and Stanisława Nowicki
why: Retrospective exhibition on the visionary Polish-American architect duo Maciej and Stanisława Nowicki, designers of the Dorton Arena, on view through March 27, 2027.

name: Exhibition: Seeing the Cinema — Photographic Visions of Movie Theaters
why: New exhibition of photographs by Hiroshi Sugimoto, Thomas R. Schiff, John Margolies, and Joseph Holmes exploring the movie theater as architectural icon and cultural form.

name: Making Art in the Era of Neurotechnology
why: MoMI LAB's inaugural artist-in-residence Rachel Rossin discusses her collaboration with Yale's Wu Tsai Institute to make art from her own brain data.

name: Greek Film Expo 2026: Michael Cacoyannis Retrospective
why: Three-day retrospective of rarely screened early films by Michael Cacoyannis (Zorba the Greek), including his 1950s breakthrough films, Oct 16–18.

name: Fantasia (1940) — Walt Disney's Animated Masterpiece
why: Screening of Walt Disney's 1940 animated masterpiece set to Bach, Tchaikovsky, Beethoven, and Stravinsky — also plays Sunday Oct 18 at 12:30pm.

name: Faust (1926) — F. W. Murnau New Restoration
why: New restoration of F. W. Murnau's 1926 silent Faust, adapting the German legend with expressionist imagery — part of the Handcrafted Horrors series.

name: Seeing the Cinema: Theaters on Screen — Goodbye, Dragon Inn
why: New ongoing series tied to the Seeing the Cinema exhibition launches Oct 30 with Tsai Ming-liang's Goodbye, Dragon Inn (2003), a meditative film set in a closing Taipei movie palace.

name: BBG Fall Harvest Festival
why: Second annual fall festival with live music and performances, cider and beer garden (NY State producers), pumpkin decorating, and afternoon costume parade, 11am–5pm. VIP tickets include tote, pint glass, and bottle opener.

name: Untapped NYC: Inwood's Hidden Power & Transit Infrastructure Tour
why: Walking tour uncovering Inwood's engineering wonders: substations, subway repair shops, and the overlooked infrastructure that keeps the city running.

name: Untapped NYC: Secrets of the Brooklyn Bridge & DUMBO Walking Tour
price: Free for Insiders/Explorers members; otherwise ticketed
why: Guided walk across the Brooklyn Bridge into DUMBO, covering hidden details of the bridge's engineering and history of the formerly industrial waterfront.

name: Untapped NYC: Powering NYC East River Ferry Tour
venue: East River Ferry (departure point via registration)
why: Ferry tour past abandoned islands, historic bridges, and massive power plants along the East River waterfront, with narration on the hidden infrastructure powering NYC.

name: Untapped NYC: Art Deco Icons of NYC Tour (Newly Enhanced Route)
why: Newly expanded Art Deco tour launching Oct 23 adding the American Radiator Building, 500 Fifth Ave, the Chanin Building lobby, and The Benjamin Hotel.

name: Untapped NYC: Gilded Age Met Museum Tour — Art & Ambition
why: Guided tour of the Metropolitan Museum discovering architectural remnants, Tiffany glass, and portraits salvaged from demolished Vanderbilt and Gilded Age mansions. Also runs Dec 12.

name: Exhibition: Cézanne to Modigliani — Gifts of Modern Art from the Pearlman Collection
why: Over 50 modern European masterpieces—including Cézanne, Degas, Gauguin, Toulouse-Lautrec, Soutine, and Modigliani—from the transformative Pearlman Collection gift to Brooklyn Museum, LACMA, and MoMA.

name: LESP OHNY Open House: Printmaking Studios & Making Strange Exhibition
venue: Lower East Side Printshop, 306 W. 37th St. (enter 307 W. 36th St.), 6th Fl.
why: OHNY open house at the Lower East Side Printshop with artist open studios, the 'Making Strange' group exhibition, and live screenprinting and linoleum-cut demos by Henry Rosenberg. Fri Oct 16 12–6pm and Sat Oct 17 12–4pm.

name: Día de los Muertos at NYBG
why: NYBG celebration of Día de los Muertos through November 2 featuring a community ofrenda, vibrant displays of marigolds and calaveras, and a larger-than-life Catrina sculpture.

name: FAQ NYC Live Recording: Immigration & Elections
why: Live recording of FAQ NYC, The City's politics podcast, with Christina Greer, Harry Siegel, Katie Honan, and Gwynne Hogan discussing how candidates talk about immigration ahead of election day. Followed by mini tours and a reception.

name: Reimagining Filipino Brooklyn
venue: Center for Brooklyn History, 128 Pierrepont Street
why: Historian Michael Menor Salgarolo and filmmaker Claro de los Reyes (screening his short 'Sands Street') explore the Filipino waterfront community around the Brooklyn Navy Yard that urban renewal all but erased.

name: We Want to Believe: UFOs, Aliens & Us
venue: Center for Brooklyn History, 128 Pierrepont Street
why: Poet and literary critic Adam Kirsch discusses 'We Want to Believe,' tracing how UFOs went from cultural punchline to subject of serious government investigation, in conversation with Christopher Beha (former Harper's editor).

name: Brooklyn Trivia with The Trivia Masters
venue: Center for Brooklyn History, 128 Pierrepont Street
why: Trivia night hosted by The Trivia Masters (Chris Kelley and Stuart Post) with Brooklyn history questions, lateral-thinking games, and multimedia rounds. Special guest: Brooklyn Borough Historian Asad Dandia.

name: Haunted Brooklyn: Ghosts, Folklore, and the Stories We Tell
venue: Center for Brooklyn History, 128 Pierrepont Street
why: Andrea Janes (Boroughs of the Dead), Leila Taylor, Colin Dickey (Ghostland), and novelist Victor LaValle discuss race, haunted places, and what Brooklyn ghost stories reveal about collective imagination.

name: Brooklyn Navy Yard Annual Open House (OHNY Weekend)
venue: Brooklyn Navy Yard — check in at Building 77, 141 Flushing Ave
why: Free OHNY open house on the 300-acre Brooklyn Navy Yard campus 12–5pm: tour artist studios, fashion/design/tech businesses, with wine tastings, food trucks, and live art demos. Two tracks: Creative Currents (artists) and BNY Past, Present & Future (space tech, robotics, green energy).

name: Masters of Horror Film Series at Quad Cinema
why: Ongoing Halloween horror series at Quad Cinema through Oct 30: Deep Red, The Fly, A Nightmare on Elm Street, Prince of Darkness, and more.

name: Hitchcocktober: Weekly Screenings at Village East by Angelika
why: Weekly Hitchcock screenings every Wednesday through Oct 31: Strangers on a Train, Rear Window, Suspicion, Vertigo, Psycho.

name: Sense + The City: A Multisensory NYC Exhibit
why: Free interactive exhibit at City Lore exploring nearly 200 NYC places through five senses: sniff scratch-and-sniff strips of sidewalk Christmas trees, touch Aqueduct racetrack dirt, hear a piano of Queens sounds. Through Jan 18, 2027.

name: Festival of Firsts at Lincoln Center (David Rubenstein Atrium)
why: Lincoln Center's fifth annual Festival of Firsts runs through Oct 23 with free performances spotlighting premieres, collaborations, and career milestones across theater, music, and dance.

name: Scientific Controversies No. 37: Octopus Umwelt
why: Pioneer Works' Science Controversies series hosts marine biologist Dr. Alex Schnell and evolutionary biologist Dr. Caroline Albertin to debate what the octopus reveals about intelligence and consciousness, hosted by PW director of sciences Janna Levin. Live cuttlefish encounter, DJ, and stargazing in the garden.

name: Little Miss Sun Sign + Q&A (The Downtown Festival) at Roxy Cinema
why: Filmmaker Joey Frank screens Little Miss Sun Sign — a film about watching Little Miss Sunshine in a manic state and setting out to recreate that epiphany — followed by Q&A. Part of the Downtown Festival.

name: False Harmonics #28: Currawong Project
price: Free for PW members; ticketed otherwise
why: Five concert pianists—Han Chen, Arseniy Gusev, Asiya Korepanova, Nicolas Namoradze, and Élisabeth Pion—rotate among three technology-enhanced grand pianos to perform Matthias Kriesberg's new work in homage to Scriabin.

name: Leenalchi + Femcel at Pioneer Works
why: Seoul-based seven-piece Leenalchi make their Brooklyn debut, fusing 17th-century Korean pansori storytelling with deep-groove psychedelia. Opened by local post-punk duo Femcel.

name: Machine Girl Halloween at Pioneer Works
why: Halloween Eve celebration with NYC electronic hardcore duo Machine Girl headlining, with support from Deli Girls and yesterdayneverhappened.

name: Kerry Kennedy with Douglas Brinkley: The Bold & Extraordinary Ethel Kennedy
venue: Stephen A. Schwarzman Building, Fifth Ave & 42nd St
why: Kerry Kennedy discusses her new biography of her mother Ethel Kennedy with historian Douglas Brinkley at the Schwarzman Building.

name: Sounds of Cyprus Presents Dialects: Greek, Turkish, and Arabic Experience
venue: Stavros Niarchos Foundation Library (SNFL), Fifth Ave & 40th St
why: Grammy-nominated musician Peter Douskalis leads Sounds of Cyprus in 'Dialects,' a multilingual concert exploring the musical traditions of Cyprus's Greek-Cypriot, Turkish-Cypriot, and Maronite-Cypriot communities.

name: Houdini: 100 Years Later — Preserving a Legacy of Magic
venue: Library for the Performing Arts, Lincoln Center
why: Marking the 100th anniversary of Houdini's death, NYPL for the Performing Arts displays rare items from his estate alongside a live escape performance by Thomas Solomon, one of today's leading escape artists. Includes a conversation with Dorothy Dietrich about her 1980 suspended straightjacket escape.

name: TechConnect Masterclass: Jam & Learn with Ableton Educators
venue: Stavros Niarchos Foundation Library (SNFL), Fifth Ave & 40th St
why: Free all-day session with Ableton Certified Trainers: keynote presentations, live jam sessions, performances, and interactive breakout sessions for musicians, producers, and teachers of all levels. 11am–4pm.

name: Home to Harlem: Celebrating Black Bibliography at the Schomburg Center
venue: Schomburg Center for Research in Black Culture, 515 Malcolm X Blvd
why: Half-day symposium at the Schomburg Center marking 100 years with archivists and scholars reconstructing founder Arturo Schomburg's personal library using physical evidence — bookplates, stamps, inscriptions. Behind-the-scenes tour included.

name: Halloween Happy Hour with Tim Gunn at NYPL
venue: Stephen A. Schwarzman Building, Fifth Ave & 42nd St
why: NYPL's annual Halloween costume parade returns: come dressed as a beloved book character, poem, or author and be judged by Tim Gunn and NYPL librarians. Historically sells out quickly.

name: Exhibition: Silly Old Bear! Winnie-the-Pooh at 100
venue: Stephen A. Schwarzman Building, Fifth Ave & 42nd St
why: Centennial display marking the 100th anniversary of Winnie-the-Pooh (first published October 1926): original A.A. Milne manuscript mockups, E.H. Shepard illustrations, rare translations, and—for the first time—the new Roo toy gifted by Queen Camilla. Through Nov 30.

name: Exhibition: Art of Manga
why: The first major manga exhibition in the Americas, featuring original art from Inuyasha, JoJo's Bizarre Adventure, Ōoku: The Inner Chambers, ONE PIECE, and dozens more — exploring manga as both popular culture and fine art. Cosplay welcome.

name: Exclusive Tour Inside the Woolworth Building
why: Recurring exclusive access tour of the Woolworth Building's ornate lobby and upper floors — Cass Gilbert's 1913 'Cathedral of Commerce,' closed to the public. Multiple dates available.

name: Inside The Players Club: Rare Look Inside Edwin Booth's Untouched Bedroom
venue: The Players Club, 16 Gramercy Park South
why: Rare access inside The Players Club, the private arts club founded by actor Edwin Booth in 1888 — including his untouched bedroom preserved exactly as he left it, the Mark Twain library, and the Booth family theater archive.

name: From Crypt to Roof: After-Hours Tour of the Cathedral of St. John the Divine
venue: Cathedral of St. John the Divine, Amsterdam Ave & 112th St
why: After-hours exploration of the world's largest Gothic cathedral from crypt to rooftop — including the Poets' Corner, biblical garden, and views of Upper Manhattan from the triforium. Halloween timing makes this especially atmospheric.

name: Grave Robbers of New York: Exploring the City's Body Snatching History
why: Halloween-season walking tour tracing NYC's 19th-century grave robbing epidemic: the body snatchers who supplied medical schools, the riots they provoked, and the forgotten burial sites now under Manhattan streets.

name: After-Hours Conservation Lab Tour at the New-York Historical Society
venue: New-York Historical Society, 170 Central Park West
why: First-ever public access to NYHS's brand-new conservation lab, where objects are cleaned, restored, and re-housed. See paintings, textiles, paper works, and three-dimensional objects in various stages of treatment.

name: Through the Mirror: Homelessness, Healthcare, and Innovation in the NYC Subways
venue: New York Transit Museum, Boerum Place & Schermerhorn St
why: Panel moderated by Vital City founder Elizabeth Glazer on NYC's subway homelessness crisis: how the City, MTA, and partners are running collaborative co-response programs to connect riders experiencing housing instability with healthcare and shelter.

name: Transit Walk: Gowanus and Carroll Gardens
why: NYTM expert-led walking tour tracing the transit history of Gowanus and Carroll Gardens — from defunct trolley lines and elevated rail remnants to the canal-side infrastructure that shaped the neighborhood's transformation.

name: NYC Secrets and Lies: Transit Tales
venue: New York Transit Museum, Boerum Place & Schermerhorn St
why: Special edition of NYC's Secrets and Lies live game show, transit edition — separate fact from fiction in a game of two truths and a lie about subway lore. Raffle for walking tour tickets if you identify the liar.

name: Subway Swing: A Boogie for the Ages
venue: New York Transit Museum, Boerum Place & Schermerhorn St
why: After-hours swing dance party inside a 1936 decommissioned subway station, with live jazz bands and a vintage dress code. Ticket includes museum admission and one drink.

name: Sinister Scents and Perfumed Potions Workshop
venue: Brooklyn Brainery (190 Underhill Ave, Prospect Heights)
why: Hands-on Halloween workshop creating custom perfumes from 'sinister' notes: decomposition, smoke, blood orange, beeswax, and other gothic botanicals. No prior experience needed.

name: Medieval Embroidered Bug Patches Workshop
venue: Brooklyn Brainery (190 Underhill Ave, Prospect Heights)
why: Embroidery workshop creating patches inspired by medieval marginalia: the beetles, snails, butterflies, and grasshoppers that 13th-century monks doodled in the margins of illuminated manuscripts.

name: Haunted History: The Age of the Witch Hunts
venue: Brooklyn Brainery (190 Underhill Ave, Prospect Heights)
why: Brooklyn Brainery Haunted History class covering the social, political, and religious forces that drove European and American witch trials — with attention to the actual accused and why the panic spread.

name: Thought Gallery Curation: American History Through Posters at Poster House
why: Private 2-hour guided tour of 'Designed to Be Red: Native American & Indigenous Poster Works' at Poster House, led by educator and printmaker Jes Hughes, covering two centuries of graphic design spanning 60 tribes and nations, followed by a hands-on letterpress workshop. Limited to 18 guests.
